source.text: וַיַּ֨עַשׂ יֹאשִׁיָּ֧הוּ בִֽירוּשָׁלִַ֛ם פֶּ֖סַח לַיהוָ֑ה וַיִּשְׁחֲט֣וּ הַפֶּ֔סַח בְּאַרְבָּעָ֥ה עָשָׂ֖ר לַחֹ֥דֶשׁ הָרִאשֽׁוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: And kept Josiah in Jerusalem [a] Passover to Yahweh, and they slaughtered the Passover on [the] fourteenth [day] of the month the first.

en.L: And Josiah kept a Passover to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in Jerusalem, and they slaughtered the Passover [lamb] on the fourteenth [day] of the first month.
en.B: Josiah kept a Passover to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in Jerusalem. They slaughtered the Passover lamb on the fourteenth day of the first month.
en.R: Josiah celebrated the Passover in Jerusalem to honor {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. The Passover lambs were killed on the fourteenth day of the first month.

decisions.choice: the Passover of 2 Kings 23:21-23, told at length
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 23:21-23 gives this Passover in three verses: the king's command to keep it "as it is written in this book of the covenant", the statement that none like it had been kept, and the date. Chronicles opens with the bare statement that Josiah kept it, tells the whole festival (verses 2-17), and then closes with the other two parts (verses 18-19). The words that match Kings are given the same wording here.

decisions.choice: the fourteenth day of the first month: the date the law sets
decisions.reason: The law sets the Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month, at evening (Exodus 12:6; Leviticus 23:5; Numbers 9:3). Hezekiah's Passover had to be held a month late, in the second month, because not enough priests were ready (30:2-3, 15). Josiah's is kept on the proper date.

decisions.choice: the Passover: the Passover animal
decisions.reason: The word names the festival in the first half of the verse and the animal killed for it in the second. The animal was a lamb or a young goat (Exodus 12:5; verse 7).

decisions.choice: [lamb] (Literal); lamb (Balanced, Readable); celebrated ... to honor (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal brackets "lamb", which the Hebrew leaves to the word "Passover"; Balanced and Readable say it. Readable says "celebrated ... to honor" for keeping a feast to the LORD, as at 2 Kings 23:21.

source.text: וַיַּעֲמֵ֥ד הַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים עַל־מִשְׁמְרוֹתָ֑ם וַֽיְחַזְּקֵ֔ם לַעֲבוֹדַ֖ת בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he appointed the priests over their duties, and he strengthened them for [the] service of [the] house of Yahweh.

en.L: And he set the priests over their duties and strengthened them for the service of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: He put the priests at their posts and urged them on in the service of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: He gave the priests their duties and encouraged them to do their work in the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: their duties: the posts each group of priests kept in turn
decisions.reason: The word means a watch or charge. The priests served by divisions, each with its own turn of duty (1 Chronicles 24:1-19; 2 Chronicles 8:14; 31:2). Josiah put each group back in its place.

decisions.choice: strengthened them: encouraged them
decisions.reason: The verb means to make strong. Said of people it means to put heart into them, as Hezekiah did for his officers (32:6-7) and David for Solomon (1 Chronicles 22:13).

decisions.choice: temple
decisions.reason: Readable says "temple" for "the house of the LORD", the plain word for the building.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לַ֠לְוִיִּם הַמְּבִינִ֨ים לְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל הַקְּדוֹשִׁ֣ים לַיהוָ֗ה תְּנ֤וּ אֶת־אֲרוֹן־הַקֹּ֨דֶשׁ֙ בַּ֠בַּיִת אֲשֶׁ֨ר בָּנָ֜ה שְׁלֹמֹ֤ה בֶן־דָּוִיד֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֵין־לָכֶ֥ם מַשָּׂ֖א בַּכָּתֵ֑ף עַתָּ֗ה עִבְדוּ֙ אֶת־יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶ֔ם וְאֵ֖ת עַמּ֥וֹ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said to the Levites who taught all Israel, the holy [ones] to Yahweh, Put [the] ark of the holiness in the house which built Solomon son of David king of Israel; there [is] no for you burden on the shoulder; now serve Yahweh your God and his people Israel.

en.L: And he said to the Levites who taught all Israel, who [were] holy to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "Put the holy ark in the house that Solomon son of David king of Israel built. There [is] no burden for you on the shoulder. Now serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people Israel.
en.B: He said to the Levites, who taught all Israel and who were holy to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "Put the holy ark in the house that Solomon son of David, king of Israel, built. You do not need to carry it on your shoulders. Serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God now, and serve {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people Israel.
en.R: Josiah spoke to the Levites. They taught all the people of Israel, and they had been set apart for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He said, "Put the holy ark in the temple that Solomon son of David, king of Israel, built. You do not have to carry it on your shoulders anymore. Now serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God and serve {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people Israel.

decisions.choice: put the holy ark in the house: the ark is to stay in its place in the temple
alternatives: the ark had been removed by an earlier king
the ark had been moved for the repairs
leave the ark where it is
decisions.reason: Solomon had placed the ark in the inner room of the temple (5:7). The text does not say why it now needed to be put there. It may have been taken out under Manasseh or Amon, when other gods were worshiped in the temple (33:4-7), or moved during the repairs (34:8-13). Or the command may mean only that it is to stay where it is, so that the Levites are free for other work.

decisions.choice: no burden on the shoulder: the Levites no longer carry the ark
decisions.reason: In the wilderness the Levites carried the ark and the holy things on their shoulders (Numbers 4:15; 7:9; 1 Chronicles 15:15). David had said that once the ark had a resting place in Jerusalem the Levites would no longer need to carry it (1 Chronicles 23:25-26). With that task gone, Josiah gives them other work: serving Yahweh and his people at the Passover.

decisions.choice: who taught: the reading in the margin
decisions.reason: The written text has a rarer form of the verb; the reading in the margin of the Hebrew text has the usual participle, "who taught". Both mean the same. The Levites taught the law to the people, as in 17:8-9 and Nehemiah 8:7-9.

decisions.choice: the holy ones to Yahweh: the Levites themselves
decisions.reason: The words stand beside "the Levites" and describe them: they were set apart for Yahweh (Numbers 3:12-13; 8:14). They are not a separate group.

decisions.choice: You do not need to carry it on your shoulders (Balanced); anymore (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced turns "there is no burden for you on the shoulder" into a plain statement about carrying the ark. Readable adds "anymore", since the carrying belonged to the past (m2).

decisions.choice: the king's speech runs from here to the end of verse 6
decisions.reason: Josiah's words to the Levites go on through verses 4-6, so the quotation opens here and closes at the end of verse 6.

source.text: וְהָכִ֥ונוּלְבֵית־אֲבוֹתֵיכֶ֖ם כְּמַחְלְקוֹתֵיכֶ֑ם בִּכְתָ֗ב דָּוִיד֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וּבְמִכְתַּ֖ב שְׁלֹמֹ֥ה בְנֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And be ready by [the] house of your fathers, by your divisions, by [the] writing of David king of Israel and by [the] document of Solomon his son.

en.L: And be ready by the houses of your fathers, by your divisions, according to the writing of David king of Israel and according to the document of Solomon his son.
en.B: Get yourselves ready by your families, in your divisions, following the written orders of David king of Israel and of his son Solomon.
en.R: Get ready in your family groups and divisions, as David king of Israel and his son Solomon wrote down.

decisions.choice: the writing of David and of Solomon: the order of the Levites set down under them
decisions.reason: David divided the Levites into groups for their work (1 Chronicles 23-26), and Solomon set them in their duties by that order (8:14). Chronicles speaks of it as something written down, so that later kings could follow it (compare 29:25).

decisions.choice: be ready: the reading in the margin
decisions.reason: The written text has "prepare"; the reading in the margin has "be ready" or "make yourselves ready". The sense is the same: the Levites are to take their places by families and divisions.

decisions.choice: the house of your fathers: your family line
decisions.reason: A "father's house" is a family group traced from a common ancestor, the unit by which the Levites were counted and served (1 Chronicles 24:4-6).

decisions.choice: houses of your fathers (Literal); families (Balanced); family groups (Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording kept for "house of fathers" since Numbers.

source.text: וְעִמְד֣וּ בַקֹּ֗דֶשׁ לִפְלֻגּוֹת֙ בֵּ֣ית הָֽאָב֔וֹת לַאֲחֵיכֶ֖ם בְּנֵ֣י הָעָ֑ם וַחֲלֻקַּ֥ת בֵּֽית־אָ֖ב לַלְוִיִּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And stand in the holy [place] by [the] divisions of [the] house of the fathers of your brothers, [the] sons of the people, and a portion of a house of a father for the Levites.

en.L: And stand in the holy [place] by the divisions of the houses of the fathers of your brothers, the sons of the people, and a portion of a father's house of the Levites [for each].
en.B: Take your stand in the holy place, family division by family division of your fellow Israelites, the lay people, with a section of a Levite family for each.
en.R: Take your places in the holy place. For each group of families of the people, there must be a group from one of the Levite families.

decisions.choice: a portion of a Levite family for each lay division
alternatives: and the Levites by the divisions of their own families
decisions.reason: The last words are short and hard. They are most easily taken to mean that each division of the lay families was to have a part of a Levite family assigned to it, to kill and prepare its lambs (verse 6). They may also mean simply that the Levites were to stand in their own family divisions.

decisions.choice: the holy place: the temple courts
decisions.reason: Here the holy place is the area of the temple where the sacrifices were made, the courts around the altar, not the inner room.

decisions.choice: your brothers, the sons of the people: the Israelites who were not Levites
decisions.reason: "Brothers" means fellow Israelites. "The sons of the people" are the lay people, as distinct from the priests and Levites (verses 7, 12, 13).

decisions.choice: [for each] (Literal); for each (Balanced, Readable); your fellow Israelites (Balanced)
decisions.reason: All three levels follow m1 and say that each division had its Levites. Balanced says "your fellow Israelites" for "your brothers", since the families included women and children; Readable leaves the phrase to "the people".

source.text: וְשַׁחֲט֖וּ הַפָּ֑סַח וְהִתְקַדְּשׁוּ֙ וְהָכִ֣ינוּ לַאֲחֵיכֶ֔ם לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת כִּדְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה בְּיַד־מֹשֶֽׁה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And slaughter the Passover, and consecrate yourselves, and prepare for your brothers, to do according to [the] word of Yahweh by [the] hand of Moses.

en.L: And slaughter the Passover [lamb], and consecrate yourselves, and prepare [it] for your brothers, to do according to the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} by the hand of Moses."
en.B: Slaughter the Passover lamb, consecrate yourselves, and prepare it for your fellow Israelites, so as to do what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said through Moses."
en.R: Make yourselves holy and kill the Passover lambs. Get them ready for your fellow Israelites. Do everything {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said through Moses."

decisions.choice: slaughter ... consecrate yourselves: two parts of one duty, not steps in order
decisions.reason: The Levites had to be ritually clean to handle the sacrifices, so "consecrate yourselves" cannot mean that they made themselves clean only after the killing. The two commands name the whole of what they must do. At Hezekiah's Passover the Levites killed the lambs for those who were not clean (30:17).

decisions.choice: by the hand of Moses: through Moses
decisions.reason: The word of Yahweh came to the people through Moses as his spokesman. The Passover laws are in Exodus 12 and Deuteronomy 16:1-8.

decisions.choice: your brothers: the lay Israelites
decisions.reason: As in verse 5, the brothers are the people of Israel, for whom the Levites prepare the Passover.

decisions.choice: Make yourselves holy and kill
decisions.reason: Readable puts the cleansing first so that it does not read as coming after the killing (m1).

source.text: וַיָּ֣רֶם יֹאשִׁיָּ֣הוּ לִבְנֵ֪י הָעָ֟ם צֹ֞אן כְּבָשִׂ֣ים וּבְנֵֽי־עִזִּים֮ הַכֹּ֣ל לַפְּסָחִים֒ לְכָל־הַנִּמְצָ֗א לְמִסְפַּר֙ שְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים אֶ֔לֶף וּבָקָ֖ר שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת אֲלָפִ֑ים אֵ֖לֶּה מֵרְכ֥וּשׁ הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And contributed Josiah to [the] sons of the people flock, lambs and young [ones] of goats, all for the Passovers, for all the [one] found, to [the] number of thirty thousand, and cattle three thousand; these [were] from [the] property of the king.

en.L: And Josiah contributed to the sons of the people [animals of the] flock, lambs and young goats, all for the Passover offerings, for all who were present, to the number of 30,000, and 3,000 cattle; these [were] from the king's property.
en.B: Josiah gave the lay people animals from the flock, lambs and young goats, all for the Passover offerings for everyone who was there, 30,000 in number, and 3,000 cattle. These came from the king's own property.
en.R: For all the people who were there, Josiah gave 30,000 lambs and young goats for the Passover offerings, and 3,000 cattle. All these came from what the king owned.

decisions.choice: contributed: set apart as a gift
decisions.reason: The verb means to lift up, and is used for setting something apart from one's own goods as an offering (Numbers 15:19-20; 2 Chronicles 30:24).

decisions.choice: cattle: for the other offerings of the festival
decisions.reason: The Passover animal itself was a lamb or a young goat (Exodus 12:5). The cattle were for the other sacrifices of the festival week, the burnt offerings and the holy offerings that were boiled and eaten (verses 12-13).

decisions.choice: the king gives from his own goods, as Hezekiah had
decisions.reason: Hezekiah gave 1,000 bulls and 7,000 sheep for his Passover, and his officials gave more (30:24). Josiah's gift is far larger. Kings also gave from their own herds for the regular offerings (31:3).
Numbers above ninety-nine are written as numerals at every level.

source.text: וְשָׂרָ֞יו לִנְדָבָ֥ה לָעָ֛ם לַכֹּהֲנִ֥ים וְלַלְוִיִּ֖ם הֵרִ֑ימוּ חִלְקִיָּ֨ה וּזְכַרְיָ֜הוּ וִֽיחִיאֵ֗ל נְגִידֵי֙ בֵּ֣ית הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים לַכֹּהֲנִ֞ים נָתְנ֣וּ לַפְּסָחִ֗ים אַלְפַּ֨יִם֙ וְשֵׁ֣שׁ מֵא֔וֹת וּבָקָ֖ר שְׁלֹ֥שׁ מֵאֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And his princes for a freewill offering to the people, to the priests and to the Levites contributed; Hilkiah and Zechariah and Jehiel, rulers of [the] house of God, to the priests gave for the Passovers two thousand and six hundred, and cattle three hundred.

en.L: And his princes contributed as a freewill offering to the people, to the priests and to the Levites. Hilkiah and Zechariah and Jehiel, rulers of the house of God, gave to the priests for the Passover offerings 2,600 and 300 cattle.
en.B: His officials also gave freely to the people, the priests and the Levites. Hilkiah, Zechariah and Jehiel, the chief officers of the house of God, gave 2,600 Passover offerings and 300 cattle to the priests.
en.R: The king's leaders also gave gifts of their own free will to the people, the priests and the Levites. Hilkiah, Zechariah and Jehiel, who were in charge of God's temple, gave the priests 2,600 lambs and goats for the Passover, and 300 cattle.

decisions.choice: his princes: the king's officials
decisions.reason: The leaders of the king's court followed his lead with gifts of their own. The next names, priests in charge of the temple, may be a group among them or a separate group.

decisions.choice: freewill offering: a gift no law required
decisions.reason: A freewill offering was given by choice, not to pay a vow or meet a rule (Leviticus 22:18-23; Deuteronomy 16:10).

decisions.choice: Hilkiah: the high priest; rulers of the house of God: the chief priests in charge of the temple
decisions.reason: Hilkiah was the high priest who found the book of the law (34:9, 14; 2 Kings 22:4, 8). The title "ruler of the house of God" is given to the chief priest in 1 Chronicles 9:11 and 2 Chronicles 31:13. Zechariah and Jehiel are not named elsewhere.

decisions.choice: princes / officials / leaders; rulers (Literal); chief officers (Balanced); were in charge (Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording kept for officials (sar) in these books. The temple title is worded as in 1 Chronicles 9:11 and 31:13: Literal keeps "rulers"; Balanced and Readable say what the men did, since "ruler" alone would suggest a king.

decisions.choice: lambs and goats
decisions.reason: Readable names the Passover animals, as verse 7 does.

source.text: וְ֠כָֽנַנְיָהוּ וּשְׁמַֽעְיָ֨הוּ וּנְתַנְאֵ֜ל אֶחָ֗יו וַחֲשַׁבְיָ֧הוּ וִיעִיאֵ֛ל וְיוֹזָבָ֖ד שָׂרֵ֣י הַלְוִיִּ֑ם הֵרִ֨ימוּ לַלְוִיִּ֤ם לַפְּסָחִים֙ חֲמֵ֣שֶׁת אֲלָפִ֔ים וּבָקָ֖ר חֲמֵ֥שׁ מֵאֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And Conaniah and Shemaiah and Nethanel his brothers, and Hashabiah and Jeiel and Jozabad, princes of the Levites, contributed to the Levites for the Passovers five thousand, and cattle five hundred.

en.L: And Conaniah, and Shemaiah and Nethanel his brothers, and Hashabiah and Jeiel and Jozabad, princes of the Levites, contributed to the Levites for the Passover offerings 5,000 and 500 cattle.
en.B: Conaniah, with his brothers Shemaiah and Nethanel, and Hashabiah, Jeiel and Jozabad, the leaders of the Levites, gave the Levites 5,000 Passover offerings and 500 cattle.
en.R: The leaders of the Levites gave the Levites 5,000 lambs and goats for the Passover, and 500 cattle. These leaders were Conaniah and his brothers Shemaiah and Nethanel, and Hashabiah, Jeiel and Jozabad.

decisions.choice: names also found under Hezekiah
decisions.reason: A Conaniah was in charge of the gifts in Hezekiah's time, with his brother Shimei, and a Shemaiah and a Jozabad served under him (31:12-15). These may be later members of the same families, since names were often handed down.

decisions.choice: Conaniah: the reading in the margin
decisions.reason: The written text and the reading in the margin differ by one letter in this name; both name the same man.

decisions.choice: the leaders of the Levites gave to the Levites
decisions.reason: Just as the king's officials gave to the priests, the chief Levites provided the animals the Levites needed for their own families and for the offerings they prepared.

decisions.choice: princes (Literal); leaders (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording kept for sar; Balanced says "leaders" since these are heads of Levite families, not court officials. Readable names the gift first and the men after it, for a shorter sentence.

source.text: וַתִּכּ֖וֹן הָעֲבוֹדָ֑ה וַיַּֽעַמְד֨וּ הַכֹּהֲנִ֧ים עַל־עָמְדָ֛ם וְהַלְוִיִּ֥ם עַל־מַחְלְקוֹתָ֖ם כְּמִצְוַ֥ת הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And was prepared the service, and stood the priests at their place and the Levites at their divisions, according to [the] command of the king.

en.L: And the service was prepared, and the priests stood at their place, and the Levites by their divisions, according to the command of the king.
en.B: So the service was made ready. The priests took their places, and the Levites stood by their divisions, as the king had commanded.
en.R: When everything was ready for the service, the priests stood in their places, and the Levites stood in their groups, as the king had ordered.

decisions.choice: the service: the work of the Passover sacrifice
decisions.reason: The word is used for the whole of the worship and work at the temple; here it is the killing, offering and cooking of the Passover told in verses 11-14. Verse 16 closes the account with the same words: "all the service of Yahweh was prepared".

decisions.choice: their place, their divisions: the places set for each group
decisions.reason: Each group had its own place and task: the priests at the altar, the Levites by their divisions among the people (verses 4-5).

decisions.choice: So
decisions.reason: Balanced opens with "So", since this verse follows from the orders and gifts of verses 3-9.

source.text: וַֽיִּשְׁחֲט֖וּ הַפָּ֑סַח וַיִּזְרְק֤וּ הַכֹּהֲנִים֙ מִיָּדָ֔ם וְהַלְוִיִּ֖ם מַפְשִׁיטִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And they slaughtered the Passover, and threw the priests from their hand, and the Levites [were] skinning.

en.L: And they slaughtered the Passover [lambs], and the priests threw [the blood received] from their hand, and the Levites [were] skinning [them].
en.B: They slaughtered the Passover lambs, and the priests splashed the blood they received from the Levites, while the Levites skinned the animals.
en.R: The Levites killed the Passover lambs and handed the blood to the priests, who splashed it on the altar. Meanwhile the Levites skinned the animals.

decisions.choice: they slaughtered: the Levites
decisions.reason: The subject is not named, but verse 6 gave the killing to the Levites, as at Hezekiah's Passover (30:17).

decisions.choice: threw from their hand: the blood, taken from the Levites' hands
decisions.reason: The object is left unsaid, as often with this verb in sacrifice: the blood was thrown or splashed against the altar (Leviticus 1:5; 3:2). "Their hand" is the Levites' hand; 30:16 says it in full: "the priests threw the blood from the hand of the Levites".

decisions.choice: skinning: preparing the carcasses
decisions.reason: Skinning the animals was work the worshiper could do (Leviticus 1:6), but at Hezekiah's dedication the Levites helped the priests with it when there were too many (29:34). Here they do it throughout.

decisions.choice: [the blood received] ... [them] (Literal); the blood, the animals (Balanced); the Levites, on the altar (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew leaves both objects unsaid. Each level supplies them, Literal in brackets; Readable also names the Levites as those who killed the lambs (m1) and the altar as where the blood went (m2).

source.text: וַיָּסִ֨ירוּ הָעֹלָ֜ה לְ֠תִתָּם לְמִפְלַגּ֤וֹת לְבֵית־אָבוֹת֙ לִבְנֵ֣י הָעָ֔ם לְהַקְרִיב֙ לַיהוָ֔ה כַּכָּת֖וּב בְּסֵ֣פֶר מֹשֶׁ֑ה וְכֵ֖ן לַבָּקָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And they removed the burnt offering to give them to [the] divisions of [the] house of fathers of [the] sons of the people, to bring near to Yahweh as written in [the] book of Moses; and so for the cattle.

en.L: And they set aside the burnt offering, to give them to the divisions of the houses of [the] fathers of the sons of the people, to offer [them] to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, as [it is] written in the book of Moses; and so [they did] with the cattle.
en.B: They set aside the burnt offerings to give them to the divisions of the families of the lay people, to offer to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, following what is written in the book of Moses. The cattle were handled in the same way.
en.R: They set aside the parts that were to be burned on the altar. They gave them to each group of families among the people, so that they could be offered to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, as the book of Moses says. They did the same with the cattle.

decisions.choice: the burnt offering: the parts of the animals to be burned on the altar
alternatives: whole burnt offerings set apart from the gifts of verses 7-9
decisions.reason: The Passover lamb was eaten by the families, not burned whole. "The burnt offering" here seems to mean the parts that belonged to Yahweh and went up in smoke on the altar, such as the fat, as with peace offerings (Leviticus 3:3-5, 14-16). It may instead mean that some of the animals given were set aside as whole burnt offerings, which the people then presented.

decisions.choice: to give them ... to offer: the lay families present the portions
decisions.reason: The portions were handed to the lay families so that each family could bring its own part near to Yahweh, as the law has the worshiper bring the fat of the peace offering in his own hands (Leviticus 7:29-30).

decisions.choice: as written in the book of Moses: the laws of sacrifice
decisions.reason: The book of Moses is the law given through him; the rules for the parts burned on the altar are in Leviticus 3 and 7.

decisions.choice: the parts that were to be burned on the altar
decisions.reason: Readable explains what was set aside, following m1. If the other reading is right, Balanced "burnt offerings" still fits.

source.text: וַֽיְבַשְּׁל֥וּ הַפֶּ֛סַח בָּאֵ֖שׁ כַּמִּשְׁפָּ֑ט וְהַקֳּדָשִׁ֣ים בִּשְּׁל֗וּ בַּסִּיר֤וֹת וּבַדְּוָדִים֙ וּבַצֵּ֣לָח֔וֹת וַיָּרִ֖יצוּ לְכָל־בְּנֵ֥י הָעָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And they cooked the Passover in the fire according to the rule, and the holy [offerings] they cooked in pots and in kettles and in pans, and brought [them] quickly to all [the] sons of the people.

en.L: And they cooked the Passover [lambs] in the fire according to the rule, and the holy [offerings] they cooked in pots and in kettles and in pans, and brought [them] quickly to all the sons of the people.
en.B: They roasted the Passover lambs over the fire according to the rule, and they boiled the holy offerings in pots, kettles and pans and quickly brought them to all the lay people.
en.R: They roasted the Passover lambs over the fire, as the law required. They boiled the other holy offerings in pots, kettles and pans. Then they hurried to serve the meat to all the people.

decisions.choice: cooked in the fire: roasted; cooked in pots: boiled
decisions.reason: The same verb is used twice. Its usual sense is to boil (1 Samuel 2:13-15), but it can mean to cook in general. Exodus 12:8-9 commands that the Passover lamb be roasted with fire and forbids eating it boiled in water, while Deuteronomy 16:7 says only "cook it". Here "in the fire, according to the rule" shows that the Passover lambs were roasted as Exodus requires, while the other holy offerings were boiled in pots, as was allowed for them (Leviticus 6:21; 1 Samuel 2:13-14). The verse uses the word of Deuteronomy in the sense of Exodus.

decisions.choice: according to the rule: Exodus 12:8-9
decisions.reason: The rule is the Passover law, which says how the lamb is to be cooked: roasted with fire, head, legs and inner parts together.

decisions.choice: the holy offerings: the other sacrifices eaten at the festival
decisions.reason: These are the sacrifices from the cattle and flocks given in verses 7-9, eaten by the worshipers, like peace offerings, during the festival.

decisions.choice: pots, kettles and pans: cooking vessels of different shapes
decisions.reason: The three words name kinds of cooking pots; their exact shapes are not known. The last is a broad, shallow dish (2 Kings 21:13).

decisions.choice: cooked ... cooked (Literal); roasted ... boiled (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the one verb twice so the reader can see it. Balanced and Readable say what the verb means in each place (m1).

decisions.choice: the other holy offerings; serve the meat
decisions.reason: Readable says "other" to make clear the holy offerings are not the Passover lambs, and "serve the meat" for what was quickly brought.

source.text: וְאַחַ֗ר הֵכִ֤ינוּ לָהֶם֙ וְלַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים כִּ֤י הַכֹּהֲנִים֙ בְּנֵ֣י אַהֲרֹ֔ן בְּהַֽעֲל֛וֹת הָעוֹלָ֥ה וְהַחֲלָבִ֖ים עַד־לָ֑יְלָה וְהַלְוִיִּם֙ הֵכִ֣ינוּ לָהֶ֔ם וְלַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים בְּנֵ֥י אַהֲרֹֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And afterward they prepared for themselves and for the priests, because the priests [the] sons of Aaron [were] in offering up the burnt offering and the fats until night; and the Levites prepared for themselves and for the priests [the] sons of Aaron.

en.L: And afterward they prepared [it] for themselves and for the priests, because the priests the sons of Aaron [were busy] offering up the burnt offering and the fat until night; so the Levites prepared [it] for themselves and for the priests the sons of Aaron.
en.B: Afterward they prepared it for themselves and the priests, since the priests, the sons of Aaron, were kept busy offering the burnt offerings and the fat until nightfall. So the Levites prepared it for themselves and for the priests, the sons of Aaron.
en.R: After that the Levites prepared the Passover for themselves and for the priests. The priests, Aaron's descendants, were busy until night offering the burnt offerings and burning the fat. That is why the Levites prepared the meal for themselves and for the priests.

decisions.choice: they prepared: the Levites prepared the Passover meal
decisions.reason: The Levites are named in the second half; "prepared" means made the Passover ready to eat, as in verse 6.

decisions.choice: until night: the work at the altar filled the day
decisions.reason: The Passover was killed toward evening and eaten that night (Exodus 12:6, 8). The priests had so many burnt offerings and fat portions to burn that they could not stop to prepare their own meal.

decisions.choice: the fat: the fat portions of the sacrifices
decisions.reason: The fat belonged to Yahweh and was burned on the altar (Leviticus 3:16-17; 7:31).

decisions.choice: [it] / [were busy] (Literal); it, were busy (Balanced); the Passover, the meal (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew leaves the object of "prepared" unsaid and has only "in offering". The other levels supply what is meant. Readable names the Levites at the start.

source.text: וְהַמְשֹֽׁרֲרִ֨ים בְּנֵי־אָסָ֜ף עַל־מַעֲמָדָ֗ם כְּמִצְוַ֤ת דָּוִיד֙ וְאָסָ֞ף וְהֵימָ֤ן וִֽידֻתוּן֙ חוֹזֵ֣ה הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְהַשֹּׁעֲרִ֖ים לְשַׁ֣עַר וָשָׁ֑עַראֵ֣ין לָהֶ֗ם לָסוּר֙ מֵעַ֣ל עֲבֹֽדָתָ֔ם כִּֽי־אֲחֵיהֶ֥ם הַלְוִיִּ֖ם הֵכִ֥ינוּ לָהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And the singers, [the] sons of Asaph, [were] at their station according to [the] command of David and Asaph and Heman and Jeduthun, the seer of the king; and the gatekeepers at gate and gate; there [was] not for them to turn from upon their service, because their brothers the Levites prepared for them.

en.L: And the singers, the sons of Asaph, [were] at their station according to the command of David and Asaph and Heman and Jeduthun the king's seer, and the gatekeepers [were] at each gate. They did not need to turn from their service, because their brothers the Levites prepared [it] for them.
en.B: The singers, the sons of Asaph, were in their places, as David, Asaph, Heman and Jeduthun the king's seer had commanded. The gatekeepers stood at each gate. They did not have to leave their posts, because their fellow Levites prepared the Passover for them.
en.R: The singers, who were descendants of Asaph, stayed in their places. This was what David had ordered, together with Asaph, Heman and Jeduthun, the king's seer. (A seer was a prophet who received messages from God.) The gatekeepers stayed at every gate. None of them had to leave their work, because the other Levites prepared the Passover for them.

decisions.choice: the singers of David's order
decisions.reason: David set Asaph, Heman and Jeduthun and their sons over the singing at the house of Yahweh (1 Chronicles 25:1-7). Asaph's descendants still served in later times (Ezra 2:41).

decisions.choice: the king's seer: a prophet who served the king
alternatives: the title for all three men
decisions.reason: A seer is a prophet, one who sees what God shows. Heman is called the king's seer in 1 Chronicles 25:5 and Asaph is called a seer in 29:30; here the title stands after Jeduthun and may belong to him or to all three.

decisions.choice: the gatekeepers at each gate: Levites who guarded the temple gates
decisions.reason: The gatekeepers were Levites who kept the temple gates day and night (1 Chronicles 9:17-27; 26:1-19).

decisions.choice: their brothers the Levites: the other Levites
decisions.reason: The singers and gatekeepers were Levites too; their fellow Levites prepared the Passover for them so that they could stay at their posts.

decisions.choice: the Passover; (A seer was a prophet who received messages from God.) (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name what was prepared, as in verse 14. Readable explains "seer" the first time it comes in a chapter (m2).

source.text: וַ֠תִּכּוֹן כָּל־עֲבוֹדַ֨ת יְהוָ֜ה בַּיּ֤וֹם הַהוּא֙ לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת הַפֶּ֔סַח וְהַעֲל֣וֹת עֹל֔וֹת עַ֖ל מִזְבַּ֣ח יְהוָ֑ה כְּמִצְוַ֖ת הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ יֹאשִׁיָּֽהוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And was prepared all [the] service of Yahweh on the day the that, to keep the Passover and to offer up burnt offerings on [the] altar of Yahweh, according to [the] command of the king Josiah.

en.L: And all the service of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was prepared on that day, to keep the Passover and to offer up burnt offerings on the altar of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, according to the command of King Josiah.
en.B: So all the service of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was made ready that day, for keeping the Passover and for burnt offerings to be offered on the altar of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, by King Josiah's command.
en.R: So that day everything was done for the service of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. The people celebrated the Passover, and burnt offerings were offered on the altar of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, just as King Josiah had ordered.

decisions.choice: all the service was prepared: the account is brought to a close
decisions.reason: The words repeat verse 10, "the service was prepared", and close the description of the day.

decisions.choice: that day: the day of the Passover sacrifice
decisions.reason: The fourteenth day of the first month (verse 1), when the lambs were killed; the festival week followed (verse 17).

decisions.choice: celebrated
decisions.reason: As in verse 1.

source.text: וַיַּעֲשׂ֨וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֧ל הַֽנִּמְצְאִ֛ים אֶת־הַפֶּ֖סַח בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֑יא וְאֶת־חַ֥ג הַמַּצּ֖וֹת שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And kept [the] sons of Israel the [ones] found the Passover at the time the that, and [the] festival of the unleavened [bread] seven days.

en.L: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel who were present kept the Passover at that time, and the festival of unleavened bread seven days.
en.B: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} who were present kept the Passover at that time, and the Festival of Unleavened Bread for seven days.
en.R: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} who were there celebrated the Passover at that time. Then they celebrated the Festival of Unleavened Bread for seven days.

decisions.choice: the festival of unleavened bread: the seven days after the Passover
decisions.reason: The festival ran from the fifteenth to the twenty-first of the month, when no leavened bread was eaten (Exodus 12:15-20; Leviticus 23:5-8).

decisions.choice: the sons of Israel who were present: all who had come
decisions.reason: The words include the people of Judah and those from the north who had come (verse 18; 34:9, 33).

decisions.choice: festival of unleavened bread (Literal); the Festival of Unleavened Bread (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As at 8:13.

source.text: וְלֹֽא־נַעֲשָׂ֨ה פֶ֤סַח כָּמֹ֨הוּ֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מִימֵ֖י שְׁמוּאֵ֣ל הַנָּבִ֑יא וְכָל־מַלְכֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל׀לֹֽא־עָשׂ֡וּ כַּפֶּ֣סַח אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂ֣ה יֹֽ֠אשִׁיָּהוּ וְהַכֹּהֲנִ֨ים וְהַלְוִיִּ֤ם וְכָל־יְהוּדָה֙ וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל הַנִּמְצָ֔א וְיוֹשְׁבֵ֖י יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And not had been kept [a] Passover like it in Israel from [the] days of Samuel the prophet; and all [the] kings of Israel not had kept like the Passover which kept Josiah, and the priests and the Levites and all Judah and Israel the [one] found, and [the] inhabitants of Jerusalem.

en.L: And no Passover like it had been kept in Israel since the days of Samuel the prophet, and none of the kings of Israel had kept [a Passover] like the Passover that Josiah kept, and the priests and the Levites and all Judah and Israel who were present, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
en.B: No Passover like it had been kept in Israel since the days of Samuel the prophet. Not one of the kings of Israel had kept such a Passover as Josiah kept with the priests and the Levites, with all Judah and the Israelites who were there, and with the people of Jerusalem.
en.R: No Passover like this one had been celebrated in Israel since the days of the prophet Samuel. None of the kings of Israel had ever celebrated a Passover like the one Josiah celebrated with the priests, the Levites, all the people of Judah and Israel who were there, and the people who lived in Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: 2 Kings 23:22, with "Samuel the prophet" for "the judges"
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 23:22 says that none like it had been kept "from the days of the judges who judged Israel". Chronicles says "since the days of Samuel the prophet", the last of the judges (1 Samuel 7:15), and names those who kept it with Josiah. The words that match Kings are given the same wording here.

decisions.choice: the kings of Israel: all the kings since the kingdom began
decisions.reason: Chronicles often uses "Israel" for the whole people. The comparison takes in Solomon and all the kings after him. Hezekiah's Passover had been the greatest since Solomon (30:26); Josiah's goes beyond it.

decisions.choice: Israel who were present: people of the old northern kingdom
decisions.reason: Josiah's reforms reached into the land of the northern tribes (34:6-7, 9, 33), and some of its people came to the Passover.

decisions.choice: as in 2 Kings 23:22
decisions.reason: Literal brackets the second "Passover", which the Hebrew leaves understood. Readable says "celebrated", as in verse 1.

source.text: בִּשְׁמוֹנֶ֤ה עֶשְׂרֵה֙ שָׁנָ֔ה לְמַלְכ֖וּת יֹאשִׁיָּ֑הוּ נַעֲשָׂ֖ה הַפֶּ֥סַח הַזֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: In [the] eighteenth year of [the] reign of Josiah was kept the Passover the this.

en.L: In the eighteenth year of the reign of Josiah this Passover was kept.
en.B: This Passover was kept in the eighteenth year of Josiah's reign.
en.R: This Passover was celebrated in the eighteenth year that Josiah was king.

decisions.choice: 2 Kings 23:23, shortened
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 23:23 reads "in the eighteenth year of King Josiah this Passover was kept to Yahweh in Jerusalem". Chronicles says "of the reign of Josiah" and leaves out "to Yahweh in Jerusalem", already said in verse 1.

decisions.choice: the eighteenth year: the year the book was found
decisions.reason: The book of the law was found and the covenant made in the same year (34:8, 14, 31), about 622 BC.

decisions.choice: celebrated ... that Josiah was king
decisions.reason: As at 2 Kings 23:23.

source.text: אַחֲרֵ֣י כָל־זֹ֗את אֲשֶׁ֨ר הֵכִ֤ין יֹֽאשִׁיָּ֨הוּ֙ אֶת־הַבַּ֔יִת עָלָ֞ה נְכ֧וֹ מֶֽלֶךְ־מִצְרַ֛יִם לְהִלָּחֵ֥ם בְּכַרְכְּמִ֖ישׁ עַל־פְּרָ֑ת וַיֵּצֵ֥א לִקְרָאת֖וֹ יֹאשִׁיָּֽהוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: After all this, when had prepared Josiah the house, went up Neco king of Egypt to fight at Carchemish on [the] Euphrates; and went out to meet him Josiah.

en.L: After all this, when Josiah had set the house in order, Neco king of Egypt went up to fight at Carchemish on the Euphrates, and Josiah went out to meet him.
en.B: After all this, when Josiah had put the temple in order, Neco king of Egypt came up to fight at Carchemish on the Euphrates River, and Josiah marched out to meet him.
en.R: Some time after Josiah had done all this and put the temple in order, Neco king of Egypt marched north to fight at Carchemish on the Euphrates River. Josiah went out to face him in battle.

decisions.choice: 2 Kings 23:29, with Carchemish named
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 23:29 says that "Pharaoh Neco king of Egypt went up to the king of Assyria, to the river Euphrates". Chronicles leaves out "Pharaoh" and the king of Assyria, and names the place he was heading for, Carchemish.

decisions.choice: Neco at Carchemish: Egypt marching north against Babylon
decisions.reason: Carchemish was a city on the upper Euphrates, on the main road between Syria and Mesopotamia. In 609 BC Neco II of Egypt marched north to help what was left of Assyria against Babylon. Four years later the Babylonians defeated Egypt at Carchemish (Jeremiah 46:2).

decisions.choice: after all this: some years after the Passover
decisions.reason: The Passover was in Josiah's eighteenth year (verse 19), about 622 BC; this battle came in 609 BC, near the end of his thirty-one years (34:1). The words pass over the years between.

decisions.choice: went out to meet him: to confront him
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 23:29, to go out "to meet" a king on the march means here to go out against him (verse 22).

decisions.choice: Some time after; marched north; to face him in battle
decisions.reason: Readable makes plain the gap in time (m3), the direction of the march, and what Josiah went out to do (m4), as Readable does at 2 Kings 23:29.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח אֵלָ֣יו מַלְאָכִ֣ים׀לֵאמֹר֩׀מַה־לִּ֨י וָלָ֜ךְ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֗ה לֹא־עָלֶ֨יךָ אַתָּ֤ה הַיּוֹם֙ כִּ֚י אֶל־בֵּ֣ית מִלְחַמְתִּ֔י וֵאלֹהִ֖ים אָמַ֣ר לְבַֽהֲלֵ֑נִי חֲדַל־לְךָ֛ מֵאֱלֹהִ֥ים אֲשֶׁר־עִמִּ֖י וְאַל־יַשְׁחִיתֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he sent to him messengers, saying, What [is] to me and to you, king of Judah? Not against you, you, the day, but against [the] house of my war; and God said to hurry me; cease for yourself from God who [is] with me, and let him not destroy you.

en.L: And he sent messengers to him, saying, "What [is there] to me and to you, king of Judah? [I come] not against you, you, this day, but against the house of my war; and God has said [for me] to hurry. Cease, for your own sake, from [opposing] God, who [is] with me, so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will not destroy you."
en.B: But Neco sent messengers to him to say, "What have I to do with you, king of Judah? I am not coming against you today, but against the house with which I am at war, and God has told me to hurry. Stop opposing God, who is with me, for your own sake, so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does not destroy you."
en.R: Neco sent messengers to tell Josiah, "King of Judah, you and I have no quarrel. I have not come to attack you today. I am at war with another kingdom, and God has told me to hurry. God is on my side. For your own good, stop fighting against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, or {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will destroy you."

decisions.choice: What to me and to you?: we have nothing to settle with each other
decisions.reason: The question is a fixed phrase meaning "there is no quarrel between us; why do you trouble me?" (Judges 11:12; 2 Samuel 16:10; 1 Kings 17:18).

decisions.choice: the house of my war: the royal house with which I am at war
decisions.reason: "House" here is a ruling house or kingdom, most likely Babylon, against which Neco was marching (verse 20). The phrase is short and unusual, but the sense is clear: Neco's war is elsewhere.

decisions.choice: against you, you: not you at all
decisions.reason: The pronoun is repeated for emphasis: Neco has not come against Josiah himself.

decisions.choice: cease from God: stop opposing God
decisions.reason: To "cease from" someone is to stop standing against him. Neco claims that God is on his side, so Josiah's march against him is a march against God.

decisions.choice: God: God himself, not "gods"
decisions.reason: The word is plural in form but takes a singular verb here, as it does when it means God. The narrator confirms in verse 22 that these words came from God (see the decision there).

decisions.choice: What [is there] to me and to you (Literal); What have I to do with you (Balanced); you and I have no quarrel (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the shape of the idiom; Balanced uses the English phrase that matches it; Readable says what it means (m1).

decisions.choice: [I come] ... [opposing] (Literal); coming, opposing (Balanced); attack, fighting against (Readable)
decisions.reason: Neco's words are clipped; each level supplies the verbs the Hebrew leaves out, Literal in brackets.

source.text: וְלֹֽא־הֵסֵב֩ יֹאשִׁיָּ֨הוּ פָנָ֜יו מִמֶּ֗נּוּ כִּ֤י לְהִלָּחֵֽם־בּוֹ֙ הִתְחַפֵּ֔שׂ וְלֹ֥א שָׁמַ֛ע אֶל־דִּבְרֵ֥י נְכ֖וֹ מִפִּ֣י אֱלֹהִ֑ים וַיָּבֹ֕א לְהִלָּחֵ֖ם בְּבִקְעַ֥ת מְגִדּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And not turned Josiah his face from him, for to fight with him he disguised himself; and not he listened to [the] words of Neco from [the] mouth of God, and he came to fight in [the] valley of Megiddo.

en.L: But Josiah did not turn his face from him, for he disguised himself to fight against him, and he did not listen to the words of Neco from the mouth of God; and he came to fight in the valley of Megiddo.
en.B: But Josiah would not turn away from him. Instead he disguised himself to fight him. He did not listen to Neco's words, which came from the mouth of God, and he went to fight in the plain of Megiddo.
en.R: But Josiah would not turn back. He put on a disguise so that he could fight Neco. He did not listen to what Neco said, even though the message came from God. Josiah went to fight in the valley of Megiddo.

decisions.choice: the words of Neco from the mouth of God: God spoke through a foreign king
decisions.reason: The narrator says plainly that Neco's warning came from God. Chronicles often shows kings brought down for not listening to God's word through a messenger (16:7-10; 25:15-16; 36:12, 15-16), and here the messenger is a foreign king. Josiah, so careful to obey the book of the law, fails to hear God speaking through an unexpected mouth, and dies for it. Huldah had promised that he would be gathered to his grave in peace and not see the disaster on Jerusalem (34:28); he dies before that disaster comes.

decisions.choice: he disguised himself: as Ahab did
decisions.reason: Ahab disguised himself before the battle at Ramoth-gilead, after refusing to heed a prophet's warning, and died from an archer's arrow, telling his driver to take him away because he was wounded (1 Kings 22:30, 34; 2 Chronicles 18:29, 33). Josiah's end follows the same pattern (verse 23).

decisions.choice: disguised himself: the Hebrew text
alternatives: he strengthened himself to fight him
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text reads "disguised himself". The ancient Greek translation reads "made himself strong" for battle, from a Hebrew verb that looks similar. The Hebrew reading is kept; it fits the echo of Ahab (m2).

decisions.choice: did not turn his face from him: would not turn back
decisions.reason: To turn one's face away is to give up a purpose; Josiah held to his plan to fight.

decisions.choice: the valley of Megiddo: the plain below the fortress
decisions.reason: Megiddo stood above the plain of the Jezreel Valley, where the coastal road came through the hills (Zechariah 12:11).

decisions.choice: even though the message came from God
decisions.reason: Readable joins the two parts of the clause with "even though" to make the narrator's point clear (m1).

source.text: וַיֹּרוּ֙ הַיֹּרִ֔ים לַמֶּ֖לֶךְ יֹאשִׁיָּ֑הוּ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ לַעֲבָדָיו֙ הַעֲבִיר֔וּנִי כִּ֥י הָחֳלֵ֖יתִי מְאֹֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And shot the archers at the king Josiah, and said the king to his servants, Take me away, for I am wounded very.

en.L: And the archers shot at King Josiah, and the king said to his servants, "Take me away, for I am badly wounded."
en.B: Archers shot at King Josiah, and he said to his officials, "Take me away, because I am badly wounded."
en.R: Archers shot arrows at King Josiah. He said to his officials, "Get me away from here! I am badly hurt."

decisions.choice: I am wounded: Ahab's words
decisions.reason: The same verb form is Ahab's cry in 1 Kings 22:34 and 2 Chronicles 18:33, "take me out, for I am wounded". The disguised king is struck by archers in both stories.

decisions.choice: take me away: carry me out of the battle
decisions.reason: The verb means to cause to pass over or away: the king asks to be moved from the fighting.

decisions.choice: servants (Literal); officials (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording kept for the king's servants in these books.

source.text: וַיַּֽעֲבִירֻ֨הוּ עֲבָדָ֜יו מִן־הַמֶּרְכָּבָ֗ה וַֽיַּרְכִּיבֻהוּ֮ עַ֣ל רֶ֣כֶב הַמִּשְׁנֶה֮ אֲשֶׁר־לוֹ֒ וַיּוֹלִיכֻ֨הוּ֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם וַיָּ֕מָת וַיִּקָּבֵ֖ר בְּקִבְר֣וֹת אֲבֹתָ֑יו וְכָל־יְהוּדָה֙ וִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם מִֽתְאַבְּלִ֖ים עַל־יֹאשִׁיָּֽהוּ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And took him his servants from the chariot, and made him ride on [the] chariot of the second which [was] to him, and brought him [to] Jerusalem, and he died and was buried in [the] graves of his fathers; and all Judah and Jerusalem [were] mourning over Josiah.

en.L: And his servants took him out of the chariot and made him ride in the second chariot that [was] his, and they brought him [to] Jerusalem, and he died and was buried in the tombs of his fathers. And all Judah and Jerusalem were mourning for Josiah.
en.B: So his officials lifted him out of the chariot, set him in the second chariot he had, and took him to Jerusalem. There he died, and he was buried in the tombs of his ancestors. All Judah and Jerusalem mourned for Josiah.
en.R: So his officials took him out of his chariot and put him in another chariot he had. They brought him to Jerusalem, and there he died. He was buried in the tombs of his ancestors. All the people of Judah and Jerusalem mourned for Josiah.

decisions.choice: he died: told differently in 2 Kings 23:30
alternatives: he died on the way to Jerusalem
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 23:29-30 says that Neco killed Josiah at Megiddo and that his servants carried him dead to Jerusalem. Chronicles tells of a wound, a second chariot, and death in Jerusalem. The order of the verbs suggests he died after reaching the city, though it may only mean he died on the way. Kings speaks briefly of the outcome; Chronicles gives the details.

decisions.choice: the second chariot: a reserve chariot
decisions.reason: A king in battle might have a spare chariot ready. It was probably larger or better suited for carrying a wounded man.

decisions.choice: the tombs of his fathers: the royal burial place
decisions.reason: Like 2 Kings 23:30 ("his own tomb"), this says he received a royal burial.

decisions.choice: officials; ancestors
decisions.reason: The wording kept for the king's servants and for "fathers" in these books.

source.text: וַיְקוֹנֵ֣ן יִרְמְיָהוּ֮ עַל־יֹאשִׁיָּהוּ֒ וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ כָֽל־הַשָּׁרִ֣ים׀וְ֠הַשָּׁרוֹת בְּקִינ֨וֹתֵיהֶ֤ם עַל־יֹאשִׁיָּ֨הוּ֙ עַד־הַיּ֔וֹם וַיִּתְּנ֥וּם לְחֹ֖ק עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְהִנָּ֥ם כְּתוּבִ֖ים עַל־הַקִּינֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And lamented Jeremiah over Josiah, and said all the singing men and the singing women in their laments about Josiah until the day, and they made them a statute in Israel; and look, they [are] written in the laments.

en.L: And Jeremiah lamented for Josiah, and all the singing men and the singing women have spoken of Josiah in their laments to this day; and they made them a rule in Israel, and look, they [are] written in the Laments.
en.B: Jeremiah sang a lament for Josiah, and all the singing men and women speak of Josiah in their laments to this day. They made them a custom in Israel, and they are written in the Laments.
en.R: Jeremiah sang a song of mourning for Josiah. To this day all the men and women who sing speak of Josiah in their songs of mourning. These songs became a custom in Israel. They are written down in the collection called the Laments.

decisions.choice: Jeremiah lamented: he made a funeral song
decisions.reason: A lament was a song for the dead, sung at a burial and afterward (2 Samuel 1:17; 3:33). Jeremiah began his work as a prophet in Josiah's thirteenth year (Jeremiah 1:2) and spoke well of him (Jeremiah 22:15-16). His lament itself is not preserved.

decisions.choice: the Laments: a collection of laments, not the book of Lamentations
decisions.reason: The book called Lamentations mourns the fall of Jerusalem, not the death of Josiah, so "the Laments" here seems to be another collection, now lost, in which songs for Josiah were written. It is possible that the writer means a collection that included Lamentations, or that later readers linked the two, but nothing in Lamentations speaks of Josiah.

decisions.choice: a statute: a fixed custom
decisions.reason: The word usually means a law or decree; here it means that the mourning for Josiah became a fixed practice, repeated year by year.

decisions.choice: to this day: the writer's own day
decisions.reason: As at 5:9, the phrase is the writer's own time, long after Josiah. Zechariah 12:11 still recalls "the mourning in the plain of Megiddo".

decisions.choice: "look" left out; custom; the Laments (Balanced); the collection called the Laments (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in the sources formula, Balanced and Readable carry the pointing word "look" by the plain statement. Readable says "collection" so that "the Laments" is not read as the book of Lamentations (m2).

source.text: וְיֶ֛תֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י יֹאשִׁיָּ֖הוּ וַחֲסָדָ֑יו כַּכָּת֖וּב בְּתוֹרַ֥ת יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] rest of [the] matters of Josiah and his steadfast loves according to [what is] written in [the] law of Yahweh,

en.L: And the rest of the matters of Josiah, and his faithful deeds according to [what is] written in the law of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}},
en.B: The rest of the acts of Josiah, and his faithful deeds in keeping with what is written in the law of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}},
en.R: Everything else Josiah did, and the faithful things he did in keeping with what is written in the law of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}},

decisions.choice: his faithful deeds: acts of loyalty to Yahweh and his law
decisions.reason: The word, in the plural, means deeds of steadfast love or loyalty. Said of a king, it means what he did in faithfulness to Yahweh. The same is said of Hezekiah (32:32) and of the deeds of loyalty to David (6:42). Here the deeds are measured by the written law, which Josiah had found and obeyed.

decisions.choice: the sentence runs on into verse 27
decisions.reason: The rest of Josiah's acts and his faithful deeds are the subject of "they are written" in verse 27.

decisions.choice: his faithful deeds (Literal, Balanced); the faithful things he did (Readable)
decisions.reason: The usual Literal "steadfast love" fits the quality, not plural deeds; all three levels say "faithful" and name them as deeds.

source.text: וּדְבָרָ֕יו הָרִאשֹׁנִ֖ים וְהָאַחֲרֹנִ֑ים הִנָּ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֔ים עַל־סֵ֥פֶר מַלְכֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וִיהוּדָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: and his matters, the first and the last, look, they [are] written on [the] book of [the] kings of Israel and Judah.

en.L: and his matters, the first and the last, look, they [are] written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah.
en.B: and his acts, from first to last, are written in the Book of the Kings of Israel and Judah.
en.R: everything he did from beginning to end, is written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah.

decisions.choice: the sources formula, in Chronicles' form; parallel to 2 Kings 23:28
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 23:28 asks, "are they not written in the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Judah?" Chronicles makes it a statement, adds "his faithful deeds" and "the first and the last", and names "the book of the kings of Israel and Judah", as at 27:7.

decisions.choice: the first and the last: his whole reign
decisions.reason: The pair of opposites takes in everything, from the beginning of his reign to its end.

decisions.choice: "look" left out; the Book of the Kings of Israel and Judah (Balanced); the book of the kings of Israel and Judah (Readable)
decisions.reason: As at 27:7: Balanced and Readable carry the pointing word by the plain statement, Balanced writes the source as a title, and Readable keeps it plain.
